name: r10-ldef-real-stel-disp
author: solx-loop
description: Exploration of the L2 end state. The store side is already at its limit: evict_last on every store is as good as any "last X MB evict_last", fractional or reordered variant (all within 1%). The real extra cost is that reads evict the dirty lines the harness flush leaves in L2. evict_first on the x loads recovers 13-15% on a read-only kernel, but with evict_last stores only 1-2% at 256-1024 tokens (8% at 586, which r6 already had). So the candidate is r6 with evict_first x loads extended from B*S
